guides.question: When is a person an Identity user versus a business profile?
problems_solved: Separates authentication identity from domain-specific person facts without duplicating credentials or forcing every contact to become a login account.
business_scenarios: An employee signs in through Identity while payroll and employment facts live in a one-to-one employee profile.
A CRM contact or customer representative with no login remains only a project-owned business Object.
use_when: A person may authenticate or bind to product-specific facts
do_not_use_when: The person is only a business contact with no governed access

guides.question: When should company structure use Identity organization units?
problems_solved: Provides one authoritative hierarchy for principal placement and organization-scoped authorization instead of copying region or department trees into projects.
business_scenarios: Regional managers access stores in their organization subtree.
Employees are placed into departments, branches, warehouses, or operating units that determine access boundaries.
use_when: Hierarchy places principals or defines organization-scoped authorization
do_not_use_when: The hierarchy is only a product taxonomy or CRM company structure

guides.question: How should Roles, exact permissions, and data scopes be modeled?
problems_solved: Converts business authority into exact operation grants and truthful row scopes instead of relying on frontend visibility or broadly named Roles.
business_scenarios: Sales representatives update only records they own while regional managers read one organization subtree.
A service Role operates only on a trusted target organization and selected menus or fields remain separately governed.
A case is visible when its related customer belongs to one of the actor's organization-scope IDs.
use_when: A confirmed Role needs exact operation authority and a truthful row boundary
do_not_use_when: The requirement is only frontend menu visibility

guides.question: When may a Business Handler create, update, disable, or resolve an Identity user?
problems_solved: Atomically delivers one Identity user, the exact manual Role set, and an optional one-to-one business-profile binding without exposing credential or session storage to project code.
business_scenarios: An employee-onboarding Operation creates a login user, assigns the approved Roles, and binds the employee profile as one idempotent delivery.
An offboarding Operation disables the user and revokes active sessions without deleting the employee's business history.
use_when: A named Business Operation must change Identity-owned user state together with its governed business effect
do_not_use_when: The request is generic Identity administration or the project only needs a non-login contact

guides.question: When may a Business Handler create or manage an Identity organization unit?
problems_solved: Creates Identity-owned authorization nodes through purpose-specific transactional contracts while preventing callers from forging hierarchy, path, ancestors, or cross-application scope.
business_scenarios: A store-opening Operation creates a store node under an authorized company and later renames or disables that same store.
A governed setup Operation creates a region, department, team, or warehouse under a persisted parent and resolves the resulting minimal projection.
use_when: A business command must deliver a real principal-placement or authorization node into Identity
do_not_use_when: The hierarchy is only business classification or ordinary organization administration already owns the change

guides.question: When should the host aggregate Workspace identity-account usage?
problems_solved: Lets installation infrastructure obtain bounded, non-PII account-category counts for host-owned metering or cleanup checks without turning the capability into a user directory or allowing callers to select arbitrary Workspaces.
business_scenarios: The host produces a metering snapshot for every authorized active Workspace using stable account categories.
A trusted cleanup workflow resolves one authority-selected Workspace's identity usage before deprovisioning.
use_when: Trusted installation infrastructure needs policy-neutral account counts with authorization audit evidence
do_not_use_when: Project code needs to search users, inspect PII, or choose another Workspace
